title: MSAA produces incorrect normals at surface edges in Forward+ renderer
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in Godot 4.7.1-stable, using the official Windows build downloaded from the Godot website.

### System information

Windows 11 - Godot v4.7.1 - Vulkan(Forward+) - Nvidia GeForce RTX 3070 Ti

### Issue description

I was developing a CompositorEffect that uses MSAA 4x and samples normals from the normal_roughness_msaa buffer, but I noticed unintended weird artifacts at the edges of curved surfaces that were not consistent with my shader's math.

When MSAA is enabled in Forward+, the normal/roughness prepass calculates sample normals for pixels that contain multiple primitives by interpolating one normal value for each triangle and assigning all samples covering that primitive to the interpolated value.

The default interpolation method uses a fixed point within the pixel for this interpolation. Notably, this interpolation point is not guaranteed to lie within the triangle being calculated. This means that for small, grazing triangles, interpolating some small distance away can result in large errors. This is especially true on smooth-shaded meshes where the vertex normals vary substantially across the projected triangle.

### Temporary Fix

Vulkan also supports centroid interpolation. This guarantees that the interpolation point lies within the triangle that will receive the normal assignment. The downside is that the interpolation points no longer have regular spacing, which can effect derivatives.
In `servers/rendering/renderer_rd/shaders/forward_clustered/scene_forward_clustered.glsl` around line 885:

```glsl
#ifdef NORMAL_USED
layout(location = 1) in vec3 normal_interp;
#endif
```

can be changed to:

```glsl
#ifdef NORMAL_USED
#ifdef MODE_RENDER_NORMAL_ROUGHNESS
layout(location = 1) centroid in vec3 normal_interp;
#else
layout(location = 1) in vec3 normal_interp;
#endif
#endif
```

to enable centroid interpolation for the normal/roughness prepass. This change fixed my edge artifacts.

I do not know how many downstream rendering systems this affects, so I am just raising this issue in case someone on the rendering team wants to take a look and decide if this change is a good/bad idea. I didn't find any Godot discussions on this issue, but I found old Unity discussions that seems to mention the problem:

https://discussions.unity.com/t/msaa-related-pixel-artifacts/891544
https://discussions.unity.com/t/jaggy-white-pixel-artifacts-on-edges-with-specular-and-antialiasing/577738/22


### Steps to reproduce

Steps to reproduce:

1. Enable Forward+ rendering and MSAA 4x.
2. Render a sphere mesh over a plane.
3. Read the multisampled normals and shade edges using differences calculated from adjacent MSAA samples.

Default interpolation:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b35170b1-a81e-4980-8ff3-7c2fd939aa43

Centroid interpolation:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d8df229b-1815-41f5-b3db-a8d56c51152d

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

My glsl and CompositorEffect code are very long and entangled with many other effects. I don't have an MRP, but hopefully the information provided is sufficient. Basically, I am using the normal angle difference between adjacent subsamples for outline detection.
